classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the sine curve and the intercepts and positive gradient of the line representing the right-hand side.

content.prompt: Which graph could be used to solve $\sin x=x-1$?

spec.description: Cosine curve and increasing line; labelled option A.
spec.mathematics: y=cos x and y=x-1; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -1 and 1; no grid.

spec.description: Sine curve and increasing line; labelled option B.
spec.mathematics: y=sin x and y=x-1; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -1 and 1; no grid.

spec.description: Cosine curve and decreasing line; labelled option C.
spec.mathematics: y=cos x and y=1-x; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -1 and 1; no grid.

spec.description: Sine curve and decreasing line; labelled option D.
spec.mathematics: y=sin x and y=1-x; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -1 and 1; no grid.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\sin x$ and $y=x-1$. The sine curve passes through the origin, rises to a maximum and crosses the horizontal axis again at $x=\pi$. The line has gradient $1$, vertical intercept $-1$ and horizontal intercept $1$. These are the two graphs shown in B.

Correct answer: B.
